headline: Highest risk is medium: Cline can write/egress from a shared workspace while dbt-core can act on warehouse data, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline has browser, filesystem, and MCP surfaces, and its workspace state is shared via filesystem; dbt-core has no documented instruction-ingest channel. The pair lacks a direct shared messaging path, so prompt injection is possible mainly through manual file handoff or shared workspace content, which is a smaller blast radius than default hijack.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace files, attacker-controlled text can cross from Cline to dbt-core inputs.
IF an operator copies Cline-generated content into dbt-core configuration or SQL without review, instruction-like payloads can propagate.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable copy-paste of generated instructions into dbt artifacts.
Review any shared file before dbt consumes it.
Use a strict template for dbt inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files, runs browsers, and has broad network egress; dbt-core touches warehouse data with allowlisted egress. If sensitive warehouse data is placed in the shared workspace or echoed into Cline outputs, leakage can occur through Cline's broader outbound surfaces. The interaction is inferred from profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF warehouse extracts or secrets are stored in the shared workspace, Cline can read them.
IF Cline forwards copied data into browser or model-provider traffic, data can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep warehouse data out of shared files.
Use separate credentials for each agent.
Redact secrets before Cline reads artifacts.
Restrict Cline network access during dbt runs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can write the filesystem and modify git state; dbt-core can call the warehouse. Their overlapping mutable surfaces create conflict if both operate on the same repo or deployment artifacts, even though dbt-core's write scope is not explicit. Uncertainty about dbt-core's local write behavior pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or generated artifacts, concurrent changes can overwrite each other.
IF dbt-core writes model outputs while Cline commits the same files, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Serialize edits to shared files.
Use separate branches per agent.
Run a quick git diff before merge.
Lock generated artifact directories.
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; dbt-core can operationalize warehouse transformations. If dbt-core treats Cline-produced SQL, docs, or model changes as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream data products. The pathway is plausible in default workflows but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes Cline-authored SQL or model files without review, incorrect logic can propagate.
IF Cline's browser-derived claims are copied into dbt documentation or tests, downstream decisions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require a human review step for Cline outputs.
Run dbt tests before deployment.
Compare generated SQL against a known-good baseline.
Limit Cline to draft-only changes.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots with broad local access, while dbt-core handles warehouse data. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy gaps rather than a clear breach. Only Cline is cited because the profile pair lacks a specific cross-border or regulated-data pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline's workspace, local handling policies may be implicated.
IF warehouse data is exported into screenshots or files, retention rules may differ across tools.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Cline workspaces.
Mask screenshots before storage.
Align retention settings for shared artifacts.
Document which system is source of record.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls.
